# Menus

Every popup menu in Playnite (the hamburger menu behind `PART_ElemMainMenu`, the top bar's sort / group / view dropdowns, the game and group context menus, the tray menu, text box menus) and every dropdown list (`ComboBox` in Settings and dialogs, Playnite's multi-select boxes) wears **one** menu design per theme, compact and drawn from its source. In most themes it was the same flat list: a 32px row, a plain hover wash, a 1px rule. Required for every new theme; existing themes are tracked in `MenuPending` in `scripts/validate-extension.ps1` until theirs lands. Worked example: **Hearthside**.

## Where it lives

The menu is the theme's default menu templates, so every menu inherits it with no switch:

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `DefaultControls/ContextMenu.xaml` | The implicit `ContextMenu` style's `Template`: the panel. Its root sets `Grid.IsSharedSizeScope="True"` and holds an `ItemsPresenter` with `KeyboardNavigation.DirectionalNavigation="Cycle"` inside a `ScrollViewer`. `GameMenu`, `GameGroupMenu` and `TrayContextMenu` are `BasedOn` this style (`scripts/templates/theme-defaults/`) |
| `Views/TopPanel.xaml` | `TopPanelMenu` (the hamburger menu and the top bar dropdowns) is `BasedOn="{StaticResource {x:Type ContextMenu}}"` and sets no `Template` of its own |
| `DefaultControls/Menu.xaml` | `{x:Static MenuItem.SubmenuItemTemplateKey}` (a plain row), `{x:Static MenuItem.SubmenuHeaderTemplateKey}` (a row with a submenu and its `Popup`, which repeats the panel), and the `{x:Static MenuItem.SeparatorStyleKey}` style's template (a group break). The `MenuItem` style's Role triggers point at the two row keys |

| `DefaultControls/ComboBox.xaml` | `PART_Popup` holds the same panel, and the `ComboBoxItem` template is a row like the menu rows (28-32px, the same highlight); the chosen item shows the theme's check mark |
| `CustomControls/ComboBoxList.xaml`, `CustomControls/FilterSelectionBox.xaml` | Optional: copies of the shared overlays (Playnite's `ComboBoxListBaseTemplate`, `FilterComboBoxListTemplate`, `FilterSelectionBoxTemplate`) with only the popup border swapped for the panel. Their rows are Playnite's check boxes |

Share the panel through one `Local...` template (Hearthside: `LocalMenuBoardTemplate` in `ContextMenu.xaml`) so menus, submenus and lists cannot drift.

Playnite builds the hamburger menu in code (`Playnite.DesktopApp.Controls.MainMenu`, a `ContextMenu`) and styles it with `TopPanelMenu`, so it changes with the rest. Top level `Menu` bars (`TopLevelHeader`, `TopLevelItem`) are not part of this.

## Compact

- Rows **28-32px** (`Height` on the row template's root; the validator checks it). The full main menu is about 19 rows and 6 breaks: it should fit in about 640px.
- A **fixed icon column** (16px icon plus an 8-12px gap), so rows with and without icons share one label edge. Never a shared-size `Auto` column that collapses when a row has no icon.
- Group breaks at most **12px** tall including the mark; panel padding at most 8px; label at the normal body font and size.
- Labels trim (`TextTrimming="CharacterEllipsis"`) rather than widen the panel. A `MinWidth` of 200-240 keeps short menus and languages from looking cramped.
- Submenu arrows and shortcuts sit at the row's right edge: the label column is a plain `*` (a `SharedSizeGroup` on a star column acts as `Auto` and leaves the arrow mid-row); only the shortcut column is shared.

## Unique: pick a signature on each lever

A theme's menu is its own when a player would recognise it with the labels blurred. Decide each lever from the source (the game's pause or options menu, the design system's menu component) and write the choice in the template header comment. Never the default trio of flat hover wash, 1px rule and grey shortcut text.

| Lever | What it can be (examples, not a menu to copy) |
|-------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Panel** (`ContextMenu` template) | Material: grained wood, stone, paper, glass, scanline CRT, holo grid. Edge: brass cap with a clasp, sawtooth paper edge, cut corners, a header band with the mark, corner brackets, a lit accent bar on one side, a hard offset shadow plate (no `DropShadowEffect`) |
| **Highlight** (the row under the pointer or keyboard) | Slab or plank, inverted key cap, slanted plate, bracket lock `[ ]`, a cursor glyph that slides in (diamond, arrow, hand, `>` prompt), an accent bar that grows, an underline sweep, a glow streak, a pixel frame swap. Animate it in (100-160 ms) and out (150-250 ms, `FillBehavior="Stop"`) |
| **Group break** (separator template) | Ornament on a tapered rule, a dotted or dashed rule, a hazard stripe, a tick ruler, a notch, plain extra space, a short rule offset to the icon column |
| **Icons** | Muted at rest and lit/inverted on highlight (`TextElement.Foreground` on `TargetName="Icon"` in `IsHighlighted` and Exit highlight triggers so icons stay legible on the hover plate; the icons themselves are the theme's own bare-icon PNG set ([Menu item icons](menu-icons.md)); PNGs do not recolour, so each icon fills the full 15-20px slot and uses a filled body + contrasting stroke or a tight contour halo — never a background badge plate — to read on both rest and hover plates; never draw a hover cursor/socket on top of an item that has an icon) |
| **Shortcuts** (F4, F6, F9, F11, F1, F3, Delete, Alt+Q) | Key caps, bracketed `[F4]`, small caps in the accent, a dot leader to the right edge, dimmed text that lights with the row |
| **Submenu mark** | The theme's chevron, a triangle, `>`, `+`, a corner fold; lit while the submenu is open, with a held (not animated) plate on the header so moving into the submenu never flickers |
| **Marked rows** | Exit is the one stable hook: `Trigger Property="InputGestureText" Value="Alt+Q"`. Give it the danger treatment (red plank, red cursor) and keep its label at 4.5:1 on that colour. Checked rows (`IsChecked`: View > Sidebar, the sort dropdown's current field) draw the theme's own check mark |

Two themes never share a row template: the validator fails a `SubmenuItemTemplateKey` template identical to another theme's. That only catches exact copies; the real test is the levers above.

## States and motion

- Highlight is `IsHighlighted` (pointer and keyboard). Animate named layers (a hover plate, a cursor, a label shift) on `Opacity` or a named `TranslateTransform` from `ControlTemplate.Triggers` only, named `BeginStoryboard`s, exit storyboards `FillBehavior="Stop"`. Layers stay `Visibility="Collapsed"` at rest, with a `DiscreteObjectKeyFrame` to `Visible` on enter and back on exit.
- `IsSubmenuOpen` on a header shows a held plate by setter, not by animation.
- `IsEnabled` False dims the row (about 0.45). Keyboard focus needs no extra ring: the highlight is the focus.
- Brushes only through `{DynamicResource}` (ThemeModifier recolours the menu). No `DropShadowEffect`, no looping animation.

## Pitfalls (found building Hearthside)

- **Star columns ignore `SharedSizeGroup`**: a `SharedSizeGroup` on a `*` column makes it `Auto`, so the submenu arrow and shortcuts stop mid-row. Keep the label column a plain `*`; share only the shortcut column.
- **Room for ornaments above the panel**: a popup clips to its child. A mark that rises above the board (Hearthside's clasp, 5px) needs a top `Margin` on the panel root (4px) and the rows pushed below it (`ScrollViewer` top margin 9). Submenu popups then shift up by the same amount (`VerticalOffset` = -(margin + row inset)) so their first row lines up with the header.
- **One panel, many hosts**: menus, submenus, `ComboBox` lists and the multi-select popups draw the same board. Put it in one `Local...` `ControlTemplate` (`TargetType="{x:Type Control}"`, `IsHitTestVisible="False"`) and host it with `<Control Template="{DynamicResource Local...}" Focusable="False" IsTabStop="False" />`.
- **Icon colour on hover (enforced by validator)**: Playnite's `Default/Media.xaml` sets `Foreground="{DynamicResource TextBrush}"` directly on its 22 icofont menu icon `TextBlock`s (and `OrangeRed`/`Yellow` on Exit/Remove/Favorites). That local value blocks `TextElement.Foreground` inheritance, leaving white icons washed out on light/inverted hover plates. Set `<Setter Property="TextElement.Foreground" Value="{DynamicResource ...}" TargetName="Icon" />` in both `SubmenuItem` and `SubmenuHeader`'s `IsHighlighted` triggers (and Exit's `MultiTrigger` / `IsSubmenuOpen` when the label colour changes). Menu icons are PNGs in every theme (`<sys:String>` paths, or NearestNeighbor `BitmapImage`s for pixel sets) ([Menu item icons](menu-icons.md)); the setter still recolours the submenu chevron and anything else in the Icon presenter.
- **Hover storyboards**: the exit storyboard has no `From` values and `FillBehavior="Stop"`; with the default `SnapshotAndReplace` handoff it takes over the enter clocks and returns to the resting values without a jump when the pointer leaves mid-animation.
- **`ComboBoxItem`**: highlight on `IsHighlighted` (pointer and keyboard), not `IsMouseOver`; pass the row colour to its `ContentPresenter` with `TextElement.Foreground="{TemplateBinding Foreground}"` so string and templated items both recolour; keep the chosen-item mark visible on its own (`IsSelected`) while another row is highlighted.
- **Multi-select boxes** (`CustomControls/ComboBoxList.xaml`, `FilterSelectionBox.xaml`): copying the overlay replaces the shared default, so keep its `Height` = `ControlHeight` styles (`FormControlHeight` rule) and Playnite's `PART_` names; change only the popup's `Border`.
- **Exit's label** on the danger plate: the highlight colour (gold, lime, cyan) usually fails 4.5:1 on red; switch it back to the plain text colour with a `MultiTrigger` (`IsHighlighted` + `InputGestureText` = `Alt+Q`).
- **`TopPanelMenu` with its own template** (Ace, Backbeat, Cloudbank, ColdSeat, Launchpad, MannCo, NightCity, Reverie): move that design into the `ContextMenu` template and make `TopPanelMenu` `BasedOn` the `ContextMenu` style with no `Template`.

## Rolling it out to a theme

1. Read the theme's `AGENTS.md`, `BRIEF.md` and `RESEARCH.md` (the source's own menus, pause screens, list pickers), and its current `ContextMenu.xaml`, `Menu.xaml`, `ComboBox.xaml`.
2. Decide every lever from the source and write it in the template header comments. It must differ from every finished row in the signatures table below.
3. Build the panel template, the two row templates, the group break, the `ComboBoxItem` row and the `ComboBox` popup; make `TopPanelMenu` plain `BasedOn`.
4. Check it: `validate-extension.ps1 -Extension <key>` with `$env:PLAYNITE_MENUS_STRICT = '<key>'` (applies the full check while the key is still in `MenuPending`), `build-theme.ps1 -Extension <key> -NoDeploy`, then `MenuRender.ps1 -Key <key> -Out <png>` and look at the PNG: rows 28-32px, arrows and shortcuts on the right edge, Exit marked, checked rows marked, labels readable on every plate.
5. Remove the key from `MenuPending` and add the theme's row to the signatures table.

## Check it

```powershell
.\scripts\validate-extension.ps1 -Extension <key>
.\scripts\build-theme.ps1 -Extension <key> -NoDeploy
C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoProfile -STA -File tests\wpf\MenuRender.ps1 -Key <key> -Out <png>
```

`MenuRender.ps1` needs Playnite installed (its 32-bit assemblies define `MainMenu`), so it runs under 32-bit Windows PowerShell and is not part of `check-all`. It builds a real `MainMenu` with Playnite's rows, a sort dropdown on `TopPanelMenu` and a game menu on the plain `ContextMenu` style, and fails when one of them misses the panel, a row at any depth or a group break misses its template, a menu or ComboBox row is outside 28-32px, or the main menu is taller than 680px. The PNG highlights Settings, opens Add Game's submenu with Exit highlighted, and draws the dropdown, the game menu and a ComboBox list beside it. Then deploy (`build-theme.ps1 -Extension <key>`), open the main menu from the sidebar and from the top bar (sidebar hidden), a top bar dropdown, a game's context menu, a Settings dropdown and an edit dialog multi-select box; hover rows, use the arrow keys, open View > Sidebar.
